children: Credit cards are clocking far more transactions than they were a year ago. But the amount being spent each time a card is used is actually getting smaller.
In July 2026, credit card transaction volumes rose 24.1 percent year-on-year to 601 million. Total credit card spending, however, grew at a much slower 7.4 percent, to Rs 2.08 lakh crore.
The result? The average amount spent per credit card transaction fell 13.5 percent from a year ago to Rs 3,460. The decline was also sharper than the 12.9 percent year-on-year fall recorded in June.
So, what is behind the smaller ticket sizes?

The Monthly Credit Card Insights: July 2026 report by Asit C. Mehta Investment Interrmediates Ltd (ACMIIL), based on RBI data, points to the continued shift towards lower-ticket RuPay credit card-linked UPI transactions.
More transactions, but smaller amounts
The numbers show how differently transaction volumes and spending are moving.

While the number of credit card transactions grew 24.1 percent over the year, the value of those transactions increased by only 7.4 percent. Average spend per transaction consequently dropped to Rs 3,460.
The report specifically links this fall to RuPay credit cards being used through UPI for lower-ticket transactions.

This is an important distinction. A RuPay credit card linked to UPI can be used to make merchant payments through UPI, instead of requiring the physical card for every transaction. The ACMIIL report, however, does not quantify how much of the industry's overall transaction growth came from credit card-linked UPI, so the data should not be read as suggesting that UPI alone drove the 24.1 percent increase.
PNB offers a glimpse of the UPI effect
There is one bank where the report provides a more direct UPI connection.

Punjab National Bank's credit card transaction volumes reached 5.2 million in July, rising another 8.9 percent month-on-month after a six-fold jump in June. ACMIIL linked this increase to the bank's Kiwi UPI partnership.

PNB's credit card spends also jumped 173 percent year-on-year and 8.6 percent month-on-month in July. But it remains a relatively small player, accounting for only 0.4 percent of industry credit card spends.
The PNB numbers provide a specific example of how UPI-linked credit card usage can push up transaction volumes, though they cannot by themselves be extrapolated to the entire industry.
Average monthly spend per card is lower too
It isn't only the amount spent in each transaction that has declined.
Average monthly spend per credit card stood at Rs 16,812 in July, up 2.2 percent from June but 2.4 percent lower than a year ago.

There are also sizeable differences across issuers. HDFC Bank recorded the highest average spend per card at Rs 22,322, followed by SBI at Rs 17,392 and ICICI Bank at Rs 17,278. The industry average was Rs 16,812.

For now, the July numbers show two trends happening together: credit cards are being used for many more transactions, while the average value of each transaction is shrinking. And according to ACMIIL, the continued move towards lower-ticket RuPay credit card-linked UPI transactions is contributing to that falling ticket size.

One thing I have deliberately not said: that UPI is definitely making people spend more frequently, or that consumers are replacing debit-account UPI with credit cards. The report doesn't establish either of those. The headline asks the question; the copy sticks to what the data can actually tell us.

title: Credit card transactions jump 24%, but average spend falls 13%. Is UPI changing how we use cards?
